beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: The method matters more than the fix. This is Risa Samanta's report — how one script renumbered every figure in a whole cancer-biology textbook.

props.command: claude "write renumber_all.py — walk each chapter's .mdx files and renumber every Figure/Video/Table caption as Chapter.Section.Index in document order"
props.segment: Renumbering a Textbook — Report by Risa Samanta

beats.role_note: the problem and stakes, BEFORE the CLI loop
beats.narration_text: A textbook's figure numbers are its wiring. As new images got added by hand, the labels drifted into a mess of styles — Figure four-dash-four-dash-two-b, five-dash-four-dash-two, seven-dash-seven-dash-four-dash-two-a — none matching the convention, and not even in order. Every reference to those figures then points at the wrong place. Fixing them one at a time across dozens of chapters is slow and error-prone. So instead of editing names by hand, the fix derives each number from where the figure actually sits in the document.
beats.visual_intent: Real drifted caption names from the actual repo animating toward a clean sectioned scheme. Show the mechanism, not a count.

beats.narration_text: The ask: write renumber_all dot py. For each chapter, walk the MDX files in order, track the current section from its heading, and renumber every Figure caption as chapter dot section dot index. Do a dry run first that prints every planned change, and only write files when I pass the word apply.

props.command:
claude "renumber_all.py:
  walk each Chapter*/**.mdx in order
  track current section from headings
  renumber captions -> Chapter.Section.Index
  DRY RUN by default; write only on 'apply'"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL renumber_all.py, trimmed to what teaches. REPLACE the code string with your real trimmed source.
beats.narration_text: Read it before you trust it. The safety is in the last lines: dry run is the default, and files are only written when the second argument is the word apply. The logic that matters is the section tracker — as it reads each file it watches the headings, so a figure's number comes from the section it's actually in, not from whatever it was called before. That's why a stray Figure 4-4-2b becomes a clean 4.5.1.

props.title: renumber_all.py
props.code: # renumber_all.py — excerpt (... = lines trimmed) TITLE_RE = re.compile(r'^title:\s*"([0-9A-Za-z]+(?:\.[0-9]+)*)\s', re.MULTILINE) FIGURE_RE = re.compile(r'(\s*Figure\s+)' + NUM + r'([^<]*)') ... def process_chapter(chapter_path, chapter_num, dry_run=True): ... for f in files: text = f.read_text(encoding='utf-8') title_match = TITLE_RE.search(text) ... section = title_match.group(1) counters = {"Figure": 0, "Video": 0, "Table": 0} ... # guard: dry run unless the caller says "apply" dry_run = (len(sys.argv) <= 2 or sys.argv[2] != "apply")
props.sparkLine: The number comes from the file's section title, not the old caption.

beats.role_note: OUTPUT (dry run) — auto-rendered card, no screen-recording. Representative captions only.
beats.narration_text: Run it dry first. Nothing is written — it just prints what it would do. Watch one transform: Figure 4-4-2b, the exact malformed name that was flagged, resolves to Figure 4.5.1. And it's section-aware, not just tidying dashes: a caption labelled Figure 4.1 sitting in the DNA-structure section correctly becomes 4.2.1. The old label never gets a vote.
beats.visual_intent: Rendered terminal-style dry-run receipt: a few old->new caption pairs, DRY RUN badge. Illustrative, not the real book.

props.caption: prints old -> new for every caption; writes nothing

beats.narration_text: The dry run looks right, so commit to it. On a fresh branch, loop the script over every chapter with the apply flag — this time it writes. A branch means the whole change is reviewable as one diff before anything merges.

props.command:
git checkout -b figure-renumbering
for ch in Chapter*; do
  python3 renumber_all.py "$ch" apply
done
git diff --stat

beats.role_note: OUTPUT (apply) — auto-rendered card, no screen-recording. Shows the apply+diff pattern.
beats.narration_text: Now the diff. Chapter after chapter, the captions line up into a single consistent scheme — chapter, section, index — and the image filenames move with them so nothing points at a stale file. One review, one branch, the whole book normalized.
beats.visual_intent: Rendered terminal card: APPLIED lines + git diff --stat summary. Illustrative, not the real book.

props.title: apply on a branch, then review the diff
props.code:
# only writes when you pass "apply"
for ch in $(ls content/docs | grep -E "^Chapter[0-9]+$" | sort -V); do
  python3 renumber_all.py "$ch" apply
done

# every change is now a reviewable diff
git diff --stat

beats.narration_text: The trick wasn't clever string editing. It was refusing to trust the old label at all — deriving every number from the figure's real position in the document. Dry-run by default kept it safe; reading the receipt caught a real collision, where a Video and a Figure had shared one counter; the apply flag made writing deliberate; and the branch made it reviewable. That's the whole pattern.
beats.visual_intent: Show the actual guard in the script: dry-run-by-default rail and the per-type counter fix that resolved the collision.

props.title: renumber_all.py — excerpt: the guards
props.code:
# 1. derive the number from position, never from the old name
section = title_match.group(1)
counters[kind] += 1

# 2. per-TYPE counter: Figure, Video and Table count separately
counters = {"Figure": 0, "Video": 0, "Table": 0}

# 3. dry-run by default: only writes when you mean it
dry_run = (len(sys.argv) <= 2 or sys.argv[2] != "apply")

# 4. run on a branch -> git diff is the review

beats.narration_text: Your turn: if you maintain structured docs, point this pattern at your own repo. Ask Claude to write a dry-run-first renumberer for your figures or tables, and make it derive each number from the heading it lives under — not from the name it already has. Run it dry, read the plan, then apply on a branch.
